tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, which left the regions on different versions. A retry finished the rollback in all regions. Now: all three regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and of the orchestrator error. Also look at why v2.3.1 went to production even though its release candidate was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

**Rollback**
- v2.3.1 was failing in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. It had been healthy before, so the change-manager approval rule didn't apply.
- The first attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, leaving the regions on different versions. I retried once and the rollback finished in all regions.
- All three regions are now on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.

**Incident**
- INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback, the orchestrator error and the current state.
- The first request to open it timed out, so I sent it again with the same key, which stops a duplicate being created. I checked afterwards and only one incident exists.

**Follow-up**
These are listed in the incident:
- Find why v2.3.1 failed.
- Find what caused the orchestrator error.
- The test version of v2.3.1 also failed in staging, yet it still went to production. That's worth looking into.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
Rollback stopped partway: us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Rolling back to a known version is safe to repeat, so I'll retry once.
